docs.title: lua-slds
docs.text:
Short Link Domain Specification — a pure Lua domain library.

SLDS defines the identity, lifecycle, and resolution semantics of short links, independent of transport, storage, caching, and security policy. The Core layer has zero external dependencies — pure Lua 5.1 / 5.3 / LuaJIT only. Infrastructure adapters (Redis, MySQL, OpenResty) are pluggable via hexagonal ports.

docs.title: Why SLDS?
docs.text:
Most short link systems couple domain logic (what a short link is) with infrastructure (HTTP, Redis, databases). SLDS separates them:

  • Core = Identity + Lifecycle + Resolution (pure Lua, no I/O)
  • Ports = Repository, Generator, Encoder (interface contracts)
  • Bundled adapters = InMemory, Base62, Sequential; hosts supply Redis/MySQL adapters when needed

This means you can swap the storage layer without touching domain logic, run the same Core in OpenResty or a plain Lua VM, and test domain rules without any external dependencies.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
luarocks install lua-slds

For source development, use luarocks make lua-slds-scm-1.rockspec to install both Core and the bundled adapters.

docs.title: Minimal Example
docs.text:
local slds = require("slds")

-- 1. Wire up adapters (ports)
local service = slds.new({
    repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository").new(),
    generator  = require("slds.adapters.sequential.generator").new(),
    encoder    = require("slds.adapters.base62.encoder").new(),
})

-- 2. Create a short link
local link = assert(service:create({}, {
    target = "https://example.com/very/long/path?query=1",
}))
print("Code:", link.code)  -- e.g., "1"

-- 3. Resolve it
local result = service:resolve({}, slds.Identity.new("default", link.code))
print("Target:", result.target)          -- "https://example.com/..."
print("Status:", result.status)          -- "ACTIVE"
print("Found:",   result.found)           -- true

-- 4. Update target
local updated = service:update({}, slds.Identity.new("default", link.code), {
    target = "https://example.com/new",
})

-- 5. Disable
local disabled = service:update({}, slds.Identity.new("default", link.code), {
    status = slds.DISABLED,
})

-- 6. Delete (terminal — cannot be restored)
local ok = service:delete({}, slds.Identity.new("default", link.code))

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Identity value object { namespace, code } — logically immutable, equality by value
  • ShortLink domain entity with lifecycle status and optional expiry
  • Lifecycle state machine: ACTIVE ↔ DISABLED → DELETED (terminal)
  • Resolution as a first-class domain operation — not just Repository.get() with extra steps
  • Ports (hexagonal): Repository, Generator, Encoder — swap implementations freely
  • Hooks for Logger/Metrics/Tracer — synchronous observers with independent payload snapshots and pcall exception isolation
  • Conformance Tests L0–L3: compatible implementations pass applicable scenarios and declare their evidence scope

Identity uses ordinary Lua tables: callers must not rewrite fields directly. Metadata table graphs are copied at domain/storage boundaries. Hooks cannot transform domain payloads; callback latency and ctx remain the host's responsibility. See the API contract.

│  Extensions: Hooks (Logger/Metrics/Tracer)           │

docs.title: slds.new(opts) -> Service
docs.text:
Static factory (dot notation). Creates a new SLDS service instance.

Parameters:

Param Type Required Description opts.repository table yes Repository port implementation opts.generator table yes Generator port implementation opts.encoder table yes Encoder port implementation opts.clock function no Function returning current timestamp (default: os.time) opts.hooks Hooks no Pre-configured Hooks instance (default: new)

Returns: Service

Errors: error(msg, 2) if any required port is missing/wrong type or clock is not a function. The clock must return a finite number. Expected port failures return nil,err; unexpected port programming errors propagate. Resolve returns a not-found result for NOT_FOUND (and legacy nil,nil absence), but propagates other repository errors without firing successful after_resolve.

docs.title: Identity.new(namespace, code) -> Identity
docs.text:
Creates a logically immutable Identity value object using an ordinary Lua table. Callers must not assign namespace/code directly; operations capture identity values and never rewrite the caller object. Update APIs reject identity changes.

Param Type Required Description namespace string yes Non-empty logical partition code string yes Non-empty short code

Errors: error(msg, 2) if namespace or code is empty/missing.

docs.title: Metamethods
docs.text:
• __eq — value equality: two identities are equal if namespace and code match.

docs.title: ShortLink.new(opts) -> ShortLink | nil, err
docs.text:
Creates a ShortLink domain entity.

Param Type Required Description opts.namespace string yes Logical partition opts.code string yes Short code opts.target string yes Destination URL (must be safe scheme) opts.status string no Lifecycle status (default: ACTIVE) opts.expires_at number no Finite Unix timestamp; equality with now is not expired opts.metadata table no Opaque raw-table snapshot (Core MUST NOT interpret)

Returns: ShortLink or nil, err with an INVALID-prefixed error for invalid target/status/expires_at/metadata. Metadata must be nil or a table; expiration must be nil or a finite number.

Errors: error(msg, 2) for programming errors (wrong types, missing required fields).

docs.title: ShortLink:is_expired(now) -> boolean
docs.text: Returns true if expires_at is set and expires_at < now.

docs.title: ShortLink:is_resolvable(now) -> boolean
docs.text: Returns true if status is ACTIVE and not expired.

docs.title: ShortLink:with_patch(patch) -> ShortLink | nil, err
docs.text:
Creates a new ShortLink with independent metadata table contents. Only non-nil target/status/expires_at fields are patched. Unsupported fields, including metadata, are ignored; nil expiration retains the previous value, and false is invalid rather than a clearing marker.

Patch Field Allowed target yes status yes (must be valid transition) expires_at yes namespace no (immutable, RULE-004) code no (immutable, RULE-004)

docs.title: ShortLink:to_table() -> table
docs.text: Returns a plain table representation with independent nested metadata tables. Construction, patching and export copy raw table graphs, including cycles and table keys; metadata metatables are omitted without invoking them. Non-table leaves retain their values; internal mutable state of functions/userdata/threads remains host-owned.

docs.title: Resolution.resolve(link, identity, now) -> ResolutionResult
docs.text:
Applies domain resolution semantics to a ShortLink.

Logic:

  1. If link is nil → not_found(identity)
  2. If status is DELETED → found=true, status=DELETED, target=nil
  3. If status is DISABLED → found=true, status=DISABLED, target=nil
  4. If expired → found=true, status=EXPIRED, target=nil
  5. If ACTIVE and not expired → found=true, status=ACTIVE, target=link.target

docs.text: Creates a "not found" result.

docs.title: Hooks.new() -> Hooks
docs.text: Creates a new hooks registry.

docs.title: Hooks:use(hook) -> Hooks
docs.text:
Registers a hook table. Chainable.

Hook table callbacks (all optional):

{
    before_create  = function(ctx, input) end,
    after_create   = function(ctx, link) end,
    before_resolve = function(ctx, identity) end,
    after_resolve  = function(ctx, result) end,
    before_update  = function(ctx, identity, patch) end,
    after_update   = function(ctx, link) end,
    before_delete  = function(ctx, identity) end,
    after_delete   = function(ctx) end,
    on_error       = function(ctx, err, callback_name) end,
}

Hooks run synchronously in registration order. Each callback receives an independent domain payload snapshot retaining domain methods; mutations cannot affect the operation, stored data, caller objects or subsequent callbacks. ctx retains its original reference and must be treated as read-only. Exceptions trigger isolated on_error callbacks without failing the operation (RULE-007/008); elapsed callback time still adds latency. This is not a timeout, execution sandbox or durable event mechanism.

docs.title: Port: slds.ports.repository
docs.text: Interface contract. Direct use throws error().

docs.title: repository:create(ctx, link) -> link, err
docs.text: Create a new short link. MUST enforce code uniqueness atomically (RULE-005).

docs.title: repository:get(ctx, identity) -> link, err
docs.text: Retrieve a short link by identity.

docs.title: repository:update(ctx, identity, patch) -> link, err
docs.text: Atomically apply supplied non-nil target/status/expires_at fields to the latest stored record, using domain validation before commit. Unspecified fields remain unchanged. Different-field updates preserve both changes; same-field updates follow commit order. A record DELETED at commit returns nil,"DELETED" unchanged. Validation failure must not partially write. Identity patches raise a programming error. A service pre-read alone does not satisfy this contract.

docs.title: repository:delete(ctx, identity) -> boolean, err
docs.text: Logical delete (set status to DELETED). Deleted codes MUST NOT be reused (RULE-006).

docs.title: generator:generate(ctx) -> id, err
docs.text: Produce an internal unique identifier. This is not the short code — the Encoder transforms it.

docs.title: encoder:encode(id) -> code
docs.text: Pure transformation from internal ID to non-empty URL-safe code. No I/O, no side effects, deterministic. The host selects a compatible Generator/Encoder pair; Core imposes no numeric ID domain, alphabet or maximum length.

docs.title: slds.adapters.inmemory.repository
docs.text:
In-memory Repository for development and testing. Stores data as data[namespace][code], preserving all valid identity tuples, including embedded NULs. Methods do not yield and are atomic within one Lua VM; this is not cross-process concurrency support. Input/returned metadata tables do not alias stored data.

local repo = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository").new()

docs.title: slds.adapters.sequential.generator
docs.text:
Sequential counter generator. Accepts integer start in [0, 9007199254740991], defaults to 1 only for nil, and guarantees increasing values only within one instance. The maximum is returned once, followed by persistent nil,"generator exhausted". Invalid starts raise a programming error.

local gen = require("slds.adapters.sequential.generator").new(1)  -- start at 1

docs.title: slds.adapters.base62.encoder
docs.text:
Base62 encoder (0-9, A-Z, a-z). Accepts only finite integers in [0, 9007199254740991]; invalid IDs raise a programming error. This range belongs to this reference adapter, not the generic port.

local enc = require("slds.adapters.base62.encoder").new()
print(enc:encode(12345))  -- "3D7"

docs.title: Operations Guide
docs.text: This guide covers production patterns, custom adapters, and operational considerations when using SLDS.

docs.title: Writing a Custom Repository Adapter
docs.text:
The Repository port defines four methods. Any implementation must satisfy the contract:

local _M = {}
_M.__index = _M

function _M.new()
    return setmetatable({}, _M)
end

function _M:create(ctx, link)
    -- MUST enforce uniqueness atomically (RULE-005)
    -- Return: link, nil on success | nil, err on conflict
end

function _M:get(ctx, identity)
    -- Return: ShortLink, nil on found | nil, Errors.NOT_FOUND on miss
end

function _M:update(ctx, identity, patch)
    -- Atomically validate and apply supplied fields to the latest record
    -- Preserve unspecified fields; reject DELETED; never partially commit
    -- Return: updated ShortLink | nil, err
end

function _M:delete(ctx, identity)
    -- Logical delete: set status = DELETED (RULE-006)
    -- Return: true, nil | nil, Errors.NOT_FOUND
end

return _M

docs.title: Redis Integration Considerations
docs.text:
SLDS does not ship a Redis adapter. A host implementation needs an unambiguous encoding of the namespace/code tuple, a serializer for its supported metadata values, connection/error handling, and atomic write operations. Concatenating arbitrary identity fields with a delimiter can collide. A Lua table cannot be passed directly as a Redis value, and a SETNX result of 0 means conflict even though 0 is truthy in Lua.

Use transactions or an equivalent server-side commit mechanism for sparse updates against the latest record. Do not implement an update as an unprotected get/modify/set sequence. Retain a tombstone after deletion so the identity remains reserved; expiring the uniqueness key would violate RULE-006.

Key rules for adapter implementations:

  1. Code uniqueness MUST be atomic (use SETNX, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT, etc.)
  2. Delete is logical (set status = DELETED), not physical removal
  3. Deleted codes MUST NOT be reusable (keep the record, reject re-creation)
  4. Repository MAY use ctx for tenant-aware queries
  5. Updates validate domain transitions and values atomically against the latest record; failures leave it unchanged
  6. Input, returned and exported metadata table snapshots must not alias stored state

docs.title: Writing a Custom Generator
docs.text:
-- Snowflake-style generator
local _M = {}
_M.__index = _M

function _M.new(worker_id)
    return setmetatable({
        worker_id = worker_id or 1,
        sequence = 0,
        last_ts = 0,
    }, _M)
end

function _M:generate(ctx)
    -- Implement snowflake logic here
    -- Return: id (number or string), nil
end

return _M

The Generator produces an internal ID, not the short code. Declare its uniqueness scope and pair it with an Encoder that accepts its ID representation and range. The bundled Base62 accepts only integers in [0, 2^53-1]; a 64-bit or string Snowflake implementation needs a compatible encoder and must not coerce IDs to inexact Lua numbers.

docs.title: Writing a Custom Encoder
docs.text:
-- Pass through IDs from a generator that already emits unique URL-safe strings.
local _M = {}
_M.__index = _M

function _M:encode(id)
    if type(id) ~= "string" or not id:match("^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$") then
        error("encoder: expected a non-empty URL-safe string ID", 2)
    end
    return id
end

return _M

The Encoder MUST be a pure transformation:

  • No I/O (no database, no network, no ngx)
  • No side effects
  • Deterministic (same input always produces same output)
  • A non-empty URL-safe string output for the supported ID domain

If an encoder can map different IDs to the same code, Repository still enforces uniqueness and returns CONFLICT. The host decides whether to retry; a truncated hash does not guarantee a collision-free mapping.

docs.title: Multi-Namespace Usage
docs.text:
Namespaces partition the short link space. Each namespace has its own code pool.

local service = slds.new({ ... })

-- Marketing namespace
service:create({ tenant = "acme" }, {
    namespace = "marketing",
    code = "bf2026",
    target = "https://shop.example.com/black-friday",
})

-- Internal namespace
service:create({ tenant = "acme" }, {
    namespace = "internal",
    code = "bf2026",  -- same code, different namespace -- no conflict
    target = "https://wiki.example.com/black-friday-plan",
})

The ctx table is passed to all port methods. Repositories MAY use it for tenant-aware data isolation.

docs.title: Logger Hook
docs.text:
local function LoggerHook(prefix)
    prefix = prefix or "[SLDS]"
    return {
        after_create = function(ctx, link)
            io.write(string.format("%s created %s/%s\n", prefix, link.namespace, link.code))
        end,
        after_resolve = function(ctx, result)
            if result.found and result.status == "ACTIVE" then
                io.write(string.format("%s resolved %s/%s -> %s\n",
                    prefix, result.namespace, result.code, result.target))
            end
        end,
        on_error = function(ctx, err, name)
            io.write(string.format("%s hook %s error: %s\n", prefix, name, err))
        end,
    }
end

service:use(LoggerHook("[APP]"))

docs.title: Metrics Hook
docs.text:
local function MetricsHook(metrics)
    return {
        after_resolve = function(ctx, result)
            metrics:increment("slds.resolve", {
                found = tostring(result.found),
                status = result.status,
            })
        end,
    }
end

Hooks are synchronous observers. SLDS isolates callback exceptions with pcall, while slow callbacks still add latency. Treat ctx as read-only and use the host's non-blocking telemetry path when needed. Measure complete operation latency in the host wrapper so repository errors are measured too; successful after_resolve callbacks do not run on infrastructure failure.

docs.title: Create with Conflict Retry
docs.text:
local function create_with_retry(service, input, max_retries)
    max_retries = max_retries or 3
    for i = 1, max_retries do
        local link, err = service:create({}, input)
        if link then return link end
        if err ~= slds.CONFLICT then
            return nil, err  -- non-conflict error, do not retry
        end
        -- Conflict -- try again (Generator will produce a new code)
        input.code = nil  -- clear custom code, let Generator produce
    end
    return nil, "max retries exceeded"
end

docs.title: Resolve with Fallback
docs.text:
local function resolve_or_fallback(service, identity, fallback_url)
    local result, err = service:resolve({}, identity)
    if not result then return nil, err end
    if result.found and result.status == "ACTIVE" then
        return result.target
    end
    return fallback_url
end

docs.title: Testing with Fake Clock
docs.text:
SLDS accepts a clock function for deterministic expiry testing:

local fake_now = 1000000
local service = slds.new({
    repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository").new(),
    generator  = require("slds.adapters.sequential.generator").new(),
    encoder    = require("slds.adapters.base62.encoder").new(),
    clock = function() return fake_now end,
})

-- Create a link that expires in 60s
local link = service:create({}, {
    target = "https://example.com",
    expires_at = fake_now + 60,
})

-- Before expiry -- resolvable
local r1 = service:resolve({}, slds.Identity.new("default", link.code))
assert(r1.found and r1.status == "ACTIVE")

-- Advance time past expiry
fake_now = fake_now + 61

-- After expiry -- not resolvable
local r2 = service:resolve({}, slds.Identity.new("default", link.code))
assert(r2.found and r2.status == "EXPIRED")  -- derived, not persisted

docs.title: Integration with OpenResty
docs.text:
SLDS Core has zero ngx dependency. Integration happens in the host layer:

location /s/:code {
    content_by_lua_block {
        local slds = require("slds")
        local service = require("app.slds_service")  -- host module returns a configured worker-local instance

        local identity = slds.Identity.new("default", ngx.var.code)
        local result, err = service:resolve({}, identity)

        if not result then
            ngx.log(ngx.ERR, "SLDS resolve failed: ", err)
            ngx.exit(503)
        elseif result.found and result.status == "ACTIVE" then
            ngx.redirect(result.target, 302)
        else
            ngx.exit(404)
        end
    }
}

The host's app.slds_service module configures a worker-local Service with suitable adapters. Lua service objects cannot be stored in ngx.shared; cross-worker persistence and uniqueness belong to the repository/generator implementation. Network connections must be acquired in a phase supported by the chosen client.

docs.title: Quick Start Tutorial
docs.text: This tutorial walks you through using SLDS from installation to a fully working short link service with InMemory adapters.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
luarocks install lua-slds

Or clone and add src/ to package.path:

git clone https://github.com/fangfengxiang/lua-slds.git
export LUA_PATH="$PWD/lua-slds/src/?.lua;$PWD/lua-slds/src/?/init.lua;;$LUA_PATH"

docs.title: 2. Wire Up Adapters
docs.text:
SLDS uses hexagonal architecture — the Core depends on ports (interfaces), not concrete implementations. You provide the implementations:

local slds = require("slds")

-- InMemory adapters are bundled for development and testing
local service = slds.new({
    repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository").new(),
    generator  = require("slds.adapters.sequential.generator").new(),
    encoder    = require("slds.adapters.base62.encoder").new(),
})
Port Role Bundled Adapter Repository Persistence (create/get/update/delete) InMemory Generator Internal ID generation Sequential counter Encoder ID → short code transformation Base62

docs.title: 3. Create a Short Link
docs.text:
-- Auto-generated code (via Generator + Encoder)
local link = assert(service:create({}, {
    target = "https://example.com/long/path?query=1",
}))
print(link.namespace)  -- "default"
print(link.code)       -- e.g., "1"
print(link.status)     -- "ACTIVE"

-- Custom code
local custom = assert(service:create({}, {
    code = "promo2026",
    target = "https://example.com/campaign",
    expires_at = os.time() + 86400 * 30,  -- 30 days
}))

Rules:

  • target is required and must be a valid URL (dangerous schemes like javascript:, data:, file: are rejected).
  • code is optional. If omitted, the Generator produces an ID and the Encoder transforms it into a short code.
  • namespace defaults to "default" if not provided.
  • expires_at is an optional Unix timestamp. If set and expires_at < now, the link is expired at resolution time.

docs.title: 4. Resolve
docs.text:
Resolution is the most important operation. It applies domain semantics (status, expiry) — it is not just a Repository.get() passthrough.

local identity = slds.Identity.new("default", "promo2026")
local result = service:resolve({}, identity)

if result.found then
    print("Target:", result.target or "(not resolvable)")
    print("Status:", result.status)
    -- Status can be: ACTIVE, DISABLED, DELETED, or EXPIRED
else
    print("Not found")
end

ResolutionResult fields:

Field Type Description found boolean Whether the identity exists in the repository namespace string Identity namespace code string Identity code target string|nil Present only if resolvable (status=ACTIVE, not expired) status string ACTIVE, DISABLED, DELETED, or EXPIRED expires_at number|nil Expiry timestamp if set

docs.title: 5. Update
docs.text:
Only mutable fields can be updated: target, status, expires_at. namespace and code are immutable (RULE-004).

-- Change target
local updated = service:update({}, identity, {
    target = "https://example.com/new-target",
})

-- Disable temporarily
local disabled = service:update({}, identity, {
    status = slds.DISABLED,
})

-- Re-enable (DISABLED → ACTIVE is allowed)
local reactivated = service:update({}, identity, {
    status = slds.ACTIVE,
})

-- Set expiry
service:update({}, identity, {
    expires_at = os.time() + 3600,  -- 1 hour
})

State transitions:

         create
           │
           ▼
       ┌────────┐  update  ┌──────────┐
       │ ACTIVE │ ◄──────► │ DISABLED │
       └────────┘          └──────────┘
           │
           │ delete
           ▼
       ┌─────────┐
       │ DELETED  │  (terminal — no transitions out)
       └─────────┘

docs.title: 6. Delete
docs.text:
Logical deletion sets status to DELETED (terminal). The record may remain in the repository for audit, but resolution returns "not resolvable". Deleted codes MUST NOT be reused (RULE-006).

local ok, err = service:delete({}, identity)
if not ok then
    print("Delete failed:", err)
end

docs.title: 7. Add Hooks
docs.text:
Hooks extend SLDS for observability without coupling to the Core. They run synchronously with independent domain payload snapshots; pcall isolates callback exceptions. Callback time adds latency, and ctx remains shared and should be treated as read-only.

local logger = {
    after_create = function(ctx, link)
        print(string.format("[LOG] Created %s/%s -> %s",
            link.namespace, link.code, link.target))
    end,
    after_resolve = function(ctx, result)
        if result.found then
            print(string.format("[LOG] Resolved %s/%s status=%s",
                result.namespace, result.code, result.status))
        end
    end,
    on_error = function(ctx, err, callback_name)
        print(string.format("[ERROR] Hook %s failed: %s", callback_name, err))
    end,
}

service:use(logger)

docs.title: 8. Error Handling
docs.text:
SLDS uses three categories of error handling:

Category Mechanism Example Runtime errors return nil, err Repository conflict, not found Programming errors error(msg, 2) Invalid argument, immutable field modification Third-party isolation pcall User hooks, injected port implementations 
-- Runtime error — check return value
local link, err = service:create({}, { target = "https://example.com" })
if not link then
    if err == slds.CONFLICT then
        print("Code already exists — try another")
    end
end

-- Programming error — will throw
local ok, err = pcall(function()
    service:update({}, identity, { code = "new-code" })
end)
-- err: "slds:update: namespace and code are immutable"

docs.text: This document indexes key architectural decisions made during SLDS development.

docs.title: Decision Index
docs.text: # Title Status Date ADR-001 Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters) Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-002 EXPIRED as Derived State (Not Persisted) Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-003 ResolutionResult Instead of ShortLink Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-004 Code Immutability After Creation Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-005 Logical Delete (No Physical Removal) Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-006 Hooks Isolation via pcall Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-007 Zero Core Dependencies (Pure Lua) Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-008 Generator/Encoder Separation Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-009 Error Handling Three-Class System Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-010 Conformance Test Suite as Specification Accepted 2026-10-08 ADR-011 Contract hardening and evidence boundaries Accepted 2026-10-18

docs.title: ADR-001: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters)
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: SLDS needs to support multiple storage backends (Redis, MySQL, in-memory) and runtime environments (plain Lua, OpenResty). The domain logic must remain stable regardless of infrastructure choices.

Decision: Use hexagonal architecture. The domain core depends on port interfaces (Repository, Generator, Encoder). Adapters implement these ports. The domain never imports an adapter directly.

Consequences: - (+) Domain logic is infrastructure-agnostic - (+) Adapters can be swapped without domain changes - (+) Domain is fully testable with mock/in-memory adapters - (-) Slightly more boilerplate (port definitions + adapter implementations)

docs.title: ADR-002: EXPIRED as Derived State (Not Persisted)
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: Short links can have an optional expires_at timestamp. When expired, resolution should return "not resolvable". Should EXPIRED be a persistent status stored in the repository, or a derived state computed at resolution time?

Decision: EXPIRED is derived at resolution time, not stored as a persistent status. Only three statuses are persisted: ACTIVE, DISABLED, DELETED.

Rationale: Storing EXPIRED as a persistent status would require: - A background scanner to periodically check and update expired records - A scheduler dependency in the domain (violates RULE-001/RULE-002) - Race conditions between the scanner and concurrent resolution

Deriving EXPIRED at resolution time (expires_at < now) is O(1), requires no background process, and is always accurate.

Consequences: - (+) No background process needed - (+) Always accurate (checked at query time) - (+) No scheduler dependency in Core - (-) expires_at must be stored and indexed if query-by-status is needed

docs.title: ADR-003: ResolutionResult Instead of ShortLink
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: The resolve operation returns link information to the caller. Should it return the internal ShortLink entity or a separate ResolutionResult?

Decision: Return ResolutionResult, a stable contract that does not expose the internal ShortLink entity.

Rationale: Returning the raw entity would leak persistence details. If ShortLink's schema changes, all consumers would break. ResolutionResult is a stable contract with a defined field set.

Consequences: - (+) Internal entity schema can evolve without breaking consumers - (+) Clear distinction between "raw data" (ShortLink) and "resolution outcome" (ResolutionResult) - (-) Extra mapping layer in Resolution.resolve()

docs.title: ADR-004: Code Immutability After Creation
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: Can the code field of a ShortLink be changed after creation?

Decision: Code is immutable after creation. The update operation rejects patches that include namespace or code.

Rationale: Changing the code would invalidate all existing short URLs pointing to the old code. It would also violate the uniqueness contract (the old code is now free, the new code might conflict). Immutability simplifies caching, indexing, and auditing.

Consequences: - (+) Short URLs are permanent once created - (+) Cache invalidation is simpler (code never changes) - (+) Audit trail is clean - (-) Cannot "rename" a short link (must delete + create new)

docs.title: ADR-005: Logical Delete (No Physical Removal)
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: When a short link is deleted, should the record be physically removed from the repository?

Decision: Delete is logical — sets status to DELETED (terminal). The record remains in the repository. Deleted codes MUST NOT be reused (RULE-006).

Rationale: - Audit trail: deleted links may need to be tracked for compliance - Collision prevention: reusing a deleted code would redirect old references to a new target - Terminal state: DELETED has no outgoing transitions in the state machine

Consequences: - (+) Full audit history - (+) No accidental code reuse - (-) Repository grows over time (needs TTL/archival policy at infrastructure level)

docs.title: ADR-006: Hooks Isolation via pcall
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: Hooks (Logger, Metrics, Tracer) are user-provided extensions. If a hook fails, should the operation fail?

Decision: Hooks are isolated via pcall. A failing hook triggers on_error callbacks without failing the operation. Callbacks remain synchronous and add latency; see ADR-011 for observer snapshots and guarantee boundaries.

Rationale: Hooks are observability extensions, not domain logic (RULE-007, RULE-008). A broken logger should not prevent a successful resolution. The pcall isolation is applied to each hook callback independently, and on_error itself is also isolated (double isolation).

Consequences: - (+) Hook exceptions do not abort operations; callback latency remains a host concern - (+) Hook exceptions are isolated; host code remains responsible for callback latency and side effects - (-) Silent failures (mitigated by on_error callback)

docs.title: ADR-007: Zero Core Dependencies (Pure Lua)
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: SLDS Core needs to run in multiple environments (plain Lua 5.1/5.3, LuaJIT, OpenResty). Should it depend on any external libraries?

Decision: Core layer has zero external dependencies. Only pure Lua stdlib is used. No ngx, redis, mysql, cjson, or any third-party Lua rock.

Rationale: A domain specification library should be as portable as possible. Depending on cjson or ngx would limit the environments where Core can run. The protocol/codec libraries that SLDS is modeled after (dkjson, lua-MessagePack) are also pure Lua.

Consequences: - (+) Maximum portability - (+) Easy to test (no mocking of external deps) - (+) Clear boundary between Core and Infrastructure - (-) Some convenience features (e.g., JSON encoding of metadata) must be done by the host

docs.title: ADR-008: Generator/Encoder Separation
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: Short code generation involves two concerns: uniqueness (ensuring no two links share a code) and encoding (producing a URL-safe string). Should these be combined into one port or separated?

Decision: Separate into two ports: Generator (produces internal unique ID) and Encoder (transforms ID to short code string).

Rationale: - Uniqueness is an infrastructure concern (needs atomicity, possibly distributed coordination) - Encoding is a pure transformation (no I/O, deterministic, mathematical) - Separation allows swapping either independently (e.g., sequential → snowflake generator, Base62 → hash encoder)

Consequences: - (+) Independent evolution of uniqueness strategy and encoding format - (+) Encoder is trivially testable (pure function) - (-) Two ports instead of one (minor complexity)

docs.title: ADR-009: Error Handling Three-Class System
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: SLDS needs a consistent error handling strategy. When should it use error() vs return nil, err vs pcall?

Decision: Three-class error handling:

  1. Runtime errors → return nil, err (repository failures, not found, conflicts)
  2. Programming errors → error(msg, 2) (invalid arguments, immutable field violation)
  3. Hook exception isolation → pcall (user hook callbacks); expected port failures return nil,err and unexpected port programming errors propagate.

Rationale: This follows the Lua ecosystem convention (lua-resty-redis, lua-resty-http, dkjson). Runtime errors are expected conditions the caller should handle. Programming errors are bugs that should fail fast. Third-party code is isolated to prevent crashes.

Consequences: - (+) Callers can distinguish "expected failures" from "bugs" - (+) Fail-fast for programming errors prevents silent corruption - (+) Hook exceptions do not fail operations; port programming errors remain visible - (-) Slightly more cognitive load (three patterns instead of one)

docs.title: ADR-010: Conformance Test Suite as Specification
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Context: SLDS is a specification, not just a library. Multiple implementations may exist (reference implementation, Redis-backed, MySQL-backed). How do we ensure they all comply?

Decision: The Conformance Test Suite (L0-L3) is the specification enforcement mechanism. Any implementation claiming SLDS compatibility MUST pass the applicable test suite (RULE-010).

Test levels:

Level Scope L0 Core: create/resolve/update/delete L1 Lifecycle: expiration, disabled, terminal delete, code reuse L2 Duplicate rejection, commit order, deterministic interleavings and atomicity; external concurrency requires adapter evidence L3 Metadata, hooks, context propagation and visibility; cache/tenant extensions require host integration evidence

Consequences: - (+) Objective compatibility verification - (+) Tests serve as executable specification - (+) New implementations can self-verify applicable scenarios and identify outstanding evidence - (-) Test suite must be maintained alongside the spec

docs.title: ADR-011: Contract hardening and evidence boundaries
docs.text:
Status: Accepted for the current reference implementation (2026-10-18).

  • Preserve ordinary Lua tables and logical identity immutability; update APIs and stored snapshots protect persistent identity, not arbitrary direct assignments.
  • Apply sparse patches atomically against the latest record using domain rules. Reject updates to DELETED at commit with nil,DELETED; different fields survive, the same field follows commit order. This does not provide application read-modify-write conflict detection.
  • Copy raw metadata table graphs on domain/storage boundaries, omit metadata metatables, and retain non-table leaves. Metadata updates and deep merge remain unsupported.
  • Hooks are synchronous observers with per-callback domain snapshots. Exception isolation is not latency isolation, sandboxing or durable delivery; ctx stays host-owned.
  • Sequential/Base62 numeric limits belong only to the bundled adapters. Generic ports remain representation-agnostic; the host selects compatible pairs.
  • Factory-driven conformance runs real reference adapters and labels sequential/interleaving evidence honestly. No real database concurrency, cache invalidation or tenant isolation claim follows from this run.
  • Every production Lua file must reach 95% line coverage independently in each supported CI interpreter. No file exclusions or stale statistics may hide a gap.

docs.title: Design Rationale
docs.text: Field Value Status Draft Created 2026-10-08

docs.title: 1. Why SLDS Exists
docs.text:
GitHub has no shortage of short link projects — but they are all too heavy. They bundle HTTP routing, database access, caching, analytics, rate limiting, and domain logic into a single monolithic codebase. There is no clean separation between what a short link IS and how it is served.

SLDS exists to define only the former:

What is the identity, lifecycle, and resolution semantics of a short link?

Everything else — HTTP, databases, caching, security, observability — is intentionally excluded from the domain specification. These are Infrastructure Adapter concerns.

Analogy: dkjson defines JSON encoding/decoding — it does not define how to serve JSON over HTTP. lua-MessagePack defines MessagePack — it does not define message queues. SLDS defines short link domain semantics — it does not define short link infrastructure.

docs.title: 2.1 Resolution ≠ Repository.get()
docs.text:
This is the most important architectural decision in SLDS.

Wrong approach:

function resolve(code)
    return repository:get(code)  -- just a passthrough
end

Right approach:

function resolve(ctx, identity)
    local link = repository:get(ctx, identity)
    if not link then
        return ResolutionResult.not_found(identity)
    end
    -- Domain decides resolvability, not the repository
    if link.status == DELETED then
        return ResolutionResult.not_resolvable(identity, DELETED)
    end
    if link.status == DISABLED then
        return ResolutionResult.not_resolvable(identity, DISABLED)
    end
    if link.expires_at and link.expires_at < clock:now() then
        return ResolutionResult.not_resolvable(identity, EXPIRED)
    end
    return ResolutionResult.resolvable(link)
end

Rationale: The domain — not the persistence layer — decides whether a link can be resolved. Resolution involves business rules (status, expiration). Repository.get() is just data retrieval. Conflating them violates the domain boundary.

Industry parallel: In DDD, a domain service encapsulates business rules that don't naturally belong to a single entity. Resolution is such a domain service.

docs.title: 2.2 Lifecycle Operations ≠ Database CRUD
docs.text:
CRUD SLDS Operation Why Different INSERT create Involves Generator + Encoder + Repository, not just a SQL INSERT SELECT resolve Domain logic (status, expiration) applied — not a raw fetch UPDATE update Only mutable fields (target, status, expires_at) — code is immutable DELETE delete Logical delete (status = DELETED), not physical row removal

Rationale: Exposing CRUD directly would leak persistence semantics into the domain. SLDS operations are lifecycle operations — they carry domain meaning, not database mechanics.

docs.title: 2.3 Status = Lifecycle Fact, Expiration = Time Condition
docs.text:
EXPIRED is not a persistent status. It is a derived state:

status (stored)    : ACTIVE | DISABLED | DELETED
status (effective)  : ACTIVE | DISABLED | DELETED | EXPIRED

Why? Because expiration is time-dependent. Storing EXPIRED would require a background job to transition ACTIVE → EXPIRED at the expiry moment. This is:

  1. Operationally complex — you need cron jobs or timers
  2. Race-prone — what if the job runs late?
  3. Reversible — what if expires_at is updated to the future? Would you need to transition EXPIRED → ACTIVE?

By making EXPIRED a derived state, SLDS avoids all these problems. The derivation happens at resolution time, which is the only time it matters.

docs.title: 2.4 Generator/Encoder = Mechanism, Not Domain
docs.text:
The Generator and Encoder are mechanisms — they produce short codes. They are NOT domain concepts.

Why separate them?

  1. Swappability: Base62 today, hash-based tomorrow, vanity codes for marketing.
  2. Testability: In tests, you can inject a deterministic generator.
  3. Extensibility: Different namespaces can use different encoders.

Industry parallel: In hexagonal architecture, the "driving" and "driven" adapters are separate from the domain. Generator and Encoder are driven adapters — the domain doesn't care how codes are produced, only that they are unique.

docs.title: 2.5 Host ≠ Identity, Domain ≠ ShortLink
docs.text:
A common mistake is to conflate the host (e.g., short.example.com) with the short link identity. SLDS explicitly separates them:

  • Host is an Application/Infrastructure concern — it determines which HTTP server handles the request.
  • Identity is { namespace, code } — it determines which short link is being resolved.

A single SLDS instance can serve multiple hosts. A single host can route to multiple SLDS namespaces. These are orthogonal concerns.

docs.title: 2.6 Core Dependency Constraints
docs.text:
Why ban ngx, redis, mysql, cjson from Core?

Because these dependencies make the Core:

  1. Non-portable — can't run in plain Lua or LuaJIT without OpenResty
  2. Non-testable — can't unit test without mocking the entire OpenResty stack
  3. Non-reusable — can't use the domain logic in a CLI tool, a migration script, or a different runtime

By restricting Core to pure Lua, SLDS becomes a true domain library that can be embedded anywhere. The Infrastructure Adapters layer adds OpenResty/Redis/MySQL when needed.

Industry parallel: dkjson has zero dependencies. lua-cjson is a C extension but the Lua interface is pure. lua-resty-http depends on ngx but explicitly separates the HTTP client from the protocol.

docs.title: 3. Boundary Judgment Methodology
docs.text:
SLDS uses a simple boundary test:

"If we remove this capability, does SLDS's Identity/Lifecycle/Resolution semantics still hold? If yes, it probably shouldn't be in Core."

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Capability Remove it? Semantics hold? In Core? Identity No N/A ✅ Yes Resolution No N/A ✅ Yes HTTP routing Yes Yes ❌ No Redis cache Yes Yes ❌ No Rate limiting Yes Yes ❌ No Click analytics Yes Yes ❌ No Metadata storage Yes Partially (but metadata is a passthrough) ✅ Yes (as passthrough) Hooks Yes Yes (hooks are optional) ✅ Yes (as extension point) Clock injection Yes Deterministic expiration checks need a time input ✅ Yes (constructor function, no additional port)

docs.title: 4. Industry Comparison
docs.text:
Project Approach SLDS Difference Polr Full-stack PHP shortener SLDS separates domain from infrastructure YOURLS Full-stack PHP shortener SLDS is a library, not an application Kutt Full-stack Node.js shortener SLDS is language-agnostic spec with Lua reference Shlink PHP shortener with REST API SLDS defines domain semantics, not REST API

SLDS's positioning is closer to specification than application:

SLDS (Specification)
  │
  ├── slds-core (Lua reference implementation)
  │
  ├── slds-conformance (test suite)
  │
  └── implementations (Redis, MySQL, OpenResty adapters)

docs.title: 5. Lua Library Design Principles Applied
docs.text: SLDS follows Lua community conventions, aligned with the lua-yar project:

docs.title: 5.1 OOP Pattern
docs.text:
-- Class-level shared metatable (Programming in Lua §16)
local _M = {}
_M.__index = _M

function _M.new(...)
    return setmetatable({...}, _M)
end

function _M:method()  -- instance method uses colon
    -- self is available
end

return _M

Not: inline setmetatable({}, {__index = Class}) (creates a new metatable per instance — deviates from standard libraries).

docs.title: 5.2 Static Factory vs Instance Method
docs.text:
• Slds.new() — dot notation (factory, no self)
  • slds:resolve(ctx, identity) — colon notation (instance method, self needed)

docs.title: 5.3 Error Handling Three-Class System
docs.text: Error Type Pattern Example Runtime error return nil, err Repository failure, not found Programming error error(msg, 2) Invalid argument type, invariant violation Third-party API pcall wrap User-provided hook callback

docs.title: 5.4 Constants Self-Managed
docs.text: Each module defines its own constants as local variables. No centralized constants module (following lua-resty-http's resty.http_const pattern). Constants are only defined when they serve a functional purpose, eliminate magic numbers, or represent a finite enumeration.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Source design discussion: docs/raw/slds-rfc-v0.1-draft.txt
  • Boundary discussion: docs/raw/slds-boundary-discussion.txt
  • Programming in Lua, Chapter 16 (Object-Oriented Programming)
  • Hexagonal Architecture (Alistair Cockburn, 2005)
  • Domain-Driven Design (Eric Evans, 2003)

docs.title: Domain Layer Architecture
docs.text: The SLDS domain layer is the heart of the system. It defines what a short link is and how it behaves, with zero dependency on infrastructure.

docs.title: Identity — Value Object
docs.text:
An Identity is the logically immutable answer to "Who is this short link?"

Identity = { namespace: string, code: string }
  • Ordinary Lua table; callers must not modify fields directly, and public update APIs reject persistent identity changes
  • Equality by value: two Identity objects with the same namespace and code are equal (__eq)
  • String representation: "namespace:code" (__tostring)

The shared class metatable supplies domain methods and value equality. The representation remains an ordinary Lua table; it does not provide a language-enforced type or read-only barrier.

docs.title: ShortLink — Domain Entity
docs.text:
A ShortLink is the mutable answer to "What does this Identity currently represent?"

ShortLink = {
    namespace:  string,
    code:       string,
    target:     string,
    status:     string,    -- ACTIVE | DISABLED | DELETED
    expires_at: number?,   -- optional Unix timestamp
    metadata:   table?,    -- opaque, Core MUST NOT interpret
}

Immutability boundary: namespace and code are immutable after creation (RULE-004). Only target, status, and expires_at can be modified via with_patch().

Target validation: The ShortLink constructor validates the target URL scheme at creation time. Dangerous schemes (javascript:, data:, file:) are rejected (Section 10.1 of RFC-0001).

docs.title: Lifecycle — State Machine
docs.text:
Three persistent statuses with a defined transition matrix:

         create
           |
           v
       +--------+  update  +----------+
       | ACTIVE | <------> | DISABLED |
       +--------+          +----------+
           |
           | delete
           v
       +---------+
       | DELETED |  (terminal)
       +---------+

EXPIRED is derived, not persisted. The Lifecycle module does not define EXPIRED as a status. It is computed at resolution time: if expires_at and expires_at < now then status = "EXPIRED". This is a critical design decision — storing EXPIRED as a persistent status would require background scanning and batch updates, coupling the domain to a scheduler.

docs.title: Resolution — Domain Operation
docs.text:
Resolution is a first-class domain operation, not an alias for Repository.get(). The distinction:

  • Repository.get(ctx, identity) retrieves raw persisted data (whatever is in storage)
  • Resolution.resolve(link, identity, now) applies domain semantics (is it active? expired? disabled? deleted?)

This separation means the domain layer decides whether a link can be resolved, while the repository merely retrieves data. A repository has no domain authority.

docs.title: ResolutionResult — Stable Contract
docs.text:
Resolution returns a ResolutionResult, not a ShortLink. This prevents domain entity leakage:

ResolutionResult = {
    found:      boolean,
    namespace:  string,
    code:       string,
    target:     string?,   -- nil if not resolvable
    status:     string,    -- ACTIVE | DISABLED | DELETED | EXPIRED
    expires_at: number?,
}

If the internal ShortLink schema changes (adds fields, renames fields), ResolutionResult remains stable. Consumers depend on the contract, not the implementation.

docs.title: 1. Zero Infrastructure Dependency
docs.text:
The domain layer imports nothing from ngx, redis, mysql, or cjson. It uses only pure Lua stdlib: string, table, math, os, pairs, ipairs, setmetatable, error, type.

This is verified by the dependency graph — all require() calls within src/slds/domain/ point only to other domain modules.

docs.title: 2. Error Handling Three-Class System
docs.text:
Category Mechanism Domain Layer Usage Runtime errors return nil, err ShortLink.new returning nil, err for invalid target Programming errors error(msg, 2) Identity.new for missing namespace Third-party isolation pcall Not used in domain layer (no third-party calls)

The domain layer is pure logic — it has no third-party calls to isolate. pcall exception isolation is used by hook dispatch; unexpected port programming errors propagate.

docs.title: 3. OOP Pattern
docs.text:
All domain objects use the standard Lua class-level shared metatable pattern:

local _M = {}
_M.__index = _M

function _M.new(...)
    return setmetatable({...}, _M)
end

Static factory methods use dot notation (Identity.new()); instance methods use colon notation (link:is_expired()). This follows the Lua ecosystem convention (lua-resty-http, dkjson, lua-MessagePack).

docs.title: Module Dependencies
docs.text:
errors.lua          <- zero dependencies (leaf module)
    ^
lifecycle.lua       <- depends on nothing (constants only)
    ^
identity.lua        <- zero dependencies (leaf module)

short_link.lua      <- depends on errors.lua, lifecycle.lua
    ^
resolution.lua      <- depends on errors.lua (for error codes)

The dependency graph is acyclic. errors.lua and lifecycle.lua are leaf modules with zero dependencies. short_link.lua and resolution.lua depend on them but not on each other.

docs.title: Ports & Adapters Architecture
docs.text: SLDS uses the Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters) pattern to isolate the domain core from infrastructure.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
Application / Host Layer
                    (HTTP, OpenResty, Auth, Cache)
                              |
                              | Identity
                              v
              +----------------------------------+
              |            SLDS Core              |
              |                                   |
              |  Domain: Identity, ShortLink,     |
              |  Lifecycle, Resolution            |
              |                                   |
              |  Service: create/resolve/         |
              |  update/delete                    |
              |                                   |
              |  Ports (interfaces):              |
              |  - Repository Port                 |
              |  - Generator Port                  |
              |  - Encoder Port                    |
              +----+----------+-----------+-------+
                   |          |           |
                   v          v           v
              +-------+  +--------+  +---------+
              | Repo  |  | Gen    |  | Encoder |
              | Impl  |  | Impl   |  | Impl    |
              +-------+  +--------+  +---------+
              InMemory   Sequential   Base62
              Redis      Snowflake    Hash
              MySQL      UUID         Custom

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Ports are interface contracts — they define what operations exist, not how they are implemented. SLDS Core depends on the port interfaces; it never imports an adapter directly.

docs.title: Repository Port
docs.text:
repository:create(ctx, link) -> link, err
repository:get(ctx, identity) -> link, err
repository:update(ctx, identity, patch) -> link, err
repository:delete(ctx, identity) -> boolean, err

Responsibilities:

Method Must Do Must NOT Do create Enforce code uniqueness atomically (RULE-005) Generate the code (that is Generator's job) get Return raw persisted data Apply resolution semantics (that is Resolution's job) update Atomically apply sparse patches to the latest record using domain validation Define different lifecycle rules or revive DELETED delete Logical delete (status = DELETED) Physically remove the record (RULE-006 requires retention)

Key principle: The repository is a persistence boundary, not a domain authority. It stores and retrieves data. It does not decide whether a link is resolvable.

docs.title: Generator Port
docs.text:
generator:generate(ctx) -> id, err

Produces an internal unique identifier — a number or string that is not yet a short code. The Encoder transforms the ID into a short code.

Why split Generator and Encoder? Separation of concerns:

  • The Generator manages uniqueness and ordering (infrastructure concern)
  • The Encoder manages human readability and URL safety (presentation concern)

The host can replace either implementation when the pair agrees on the ID representation and range. A string/UUID generator is not automatically compatible with the bundled numeric Base62 encoder. The generic ports impose no bundled numeric range or maximum code length.

docs.title: Encoder Port
docs.text:
encoder:encode(id) -> code

A pure transformation — no I/O, no side effects, deterministic. The same input always produces the same output.

Constraints:

  • MUST NOT take ctx (no context needed for a pure function)
  • MUST NOT access network, database, or ngx
  • MUST produce a URL-safe string

docs.title: Adapters
docs.text: Adapters are implementations of ports. SLDS bundles three reference adapters for development and testing. Production adapters (Redis, MySQL, Snowflake) are implemented by the application layer.

docs.title: Bundled Adapters
docs.text: Adapter Port Use Case adapters/inmemory/repository Repository Development, testing, Conformance Test Suite adapters/sequential/generator Generator Development, testing (simple incrementing counter) adapters/base62/encoder Encoder Production-ready (0-9, A-Z, a-z = 62 chars)

docs.title: InMemory Repository
docs.text: Stores data as data[namespace][code], distinguishing even identity tuples containing NUL. Metadata tables are snapshotted on input and output. Create/update/delete do not yield; update validates and commits against the latest record within one Lua VM. Logical deletion retains the record and its uniqueness reservation. This is not a cross-process locking mechanism.

docs.title: Sequential Generator
docs.text: A simple counter starting at 1 by default, with an explicit integer domain [0, 9007199254740991]. Uniqueness is per instance, not distributed. The maximum is returned once; subsequent generation returns nil,"generator exhausted". Host-selected production generators must be paired with a compatible encoder.

docs.title: Base62 Encoder
docs.text:
Converts a finite integer in [0, 9007199254740991] to a Base62 string; this is an adapter-specific range:

0  -> "0"
1  -> "1"
10 -> "A"
61 -> "z"
62 -> "10"

The character set is 0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz.

docs.title: Dependency Direction
docs.text:
Domain  -->  Ports  -->  (nothing)
                    ^
                    |
Adapters  -->  Ports (implements)

The dependency rule: dependencies point inward. The domain layer depends on port interfaces. Adapters depend on the same port interfaces. The domain never depends on adapters. The host application wires adapters to the domain through the service constructor.

docs.title: Context (ctx)
docs.text:
The ctx parameter flows through all port methods. It is not a domain concept — it is an API/Port parameter:

  • The domain layer treats ctx as an opaque table
  • Adapters MAY use ctx for tenant-aware queries, trace propagation, or auth context
  • The host application populates ctx before calling service operations

This design allows multi-tenant isolation without the domain layer knowing about tenants.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
The hexagonal architecture enables comprehensive testing at each layer:

Test Layer What is Tested Adapters Used Domain unit tests Domain logic (Identity, ShortLink, Lifecycle, Resolution) None (pure logic) Service tests Orchestration, hooks, error mapping Real reference adapters; targeted fault injection Conformance L0-L1 Core operations and lifecycle semantics InMemory adapters Conformance L2 Sequential reliability and deterministic update/delete interleavings InMemory; real concurrency requires external adapter evidence Conformance L3 Metadata, observer hooks, context propagation and visibility InMemory; tenant/cache extensions are not applicable External integration tests Real infrastructure concurrency, optional cache/tenant behavior Supplied by adapter authors, not claimed by the reference suite

The Conformance Test Suite (L0-L3) is the specification enforcement mechanism (RULE-010). Any implementation claiming SLDS compatibility MUST pass it.

docs.title: RFC-0001: SLDS v0.1 — Short Link Domain Specification
docs.text: Field Value Status Draft Version 0.1.0 Created 2026-10-08 Language Lua 5.1 / 5.3 / LuaJIT

docs.title: 1. Abstract
docs.text:
SLDS (Short Link Domain Specification) defines the identity, lifecycle, and resolution semantics of short links, while remaining independent of transport, storage, caching, security policy, observability, analytics, and deployment.

Compressed definition:

SLDS = Short Link Identity + Lifecycle + Resolution Semantics

SLDS is a pure Lua domain library — analogous to how dkjson is a JSON codec or lua-MessagePack is a MessagePack codec. It does not concern itself with HTTP routing, database access, Redis caching, or OpenResty integration. Those are Infrastructure Adapter concerns, layered on top of SLDS.

docs.title: 2. Iron Rules
docs.text:
These ten rules are the soul of the project. They MUST be placed at the very front of any implementation.

Rule Statement RULE-001 SLDS Core MUST NOT depend on HTTP. RULE-002 SLDS Core MUST NOT depend on a specific database. RULE-003 SLDS Core MUST NOT fetch Target URLs. RULE-004 Code MUST be immutable after creation. RULE-005 Code uniqueness MUST be enforced atomically by the persistence layer. RULE-006 Deleted Codes MUST NOT be reused by default. RULE-007 Resolve MUST NOT require an external event/analytics system to succeed. RULE-008 Analytics MUST NOT be part of the resolution critical path. RULE-009 Authorization MUST be implemented outside the Core Domain. RULE-010 Any implementation claiming SLDS compatibility MUST pass the applicable Conformance Test Suite.

docs.title: 3.1 Identity
docs.text:
The Identity answers the question: "Who is this short link?"

Identity = { namespace, code }
  • namespace — logical partition (e.g., "default", "marketing", "internal")
  • code — the short code string (e.g., "a8Kx2")

Identity is NOT: URL, Host, Domain, Tenant, User, Campaign, Database ID, or Redis Key. It is the minimal tuple that uniquely identifies a short link within the domain.

Identity is a value object — logically immutable after creation. Its Lua reference representation is an ordinary table: callers MUST NOT rewrite its fields, and operations MUST NOT mutate the caller object. Update APIs prohibit persistent identity changes; direct-assignment errors are not promised. Two Identity objects with the same namespace/code are equal.

docs.title: 3.2 ShortLink
docs.text:
The ShortLink answers the question: "What does this Identity currently represent?"

ShortLink = { namespace, code, target, status, expires_at }
  • target — the destination URL string
  • status — lifecycle status (see §3.3)
  • expires_at — optional Unix timestamp; if set and expires_at < now, the link is considered expired

docs.title: 3.3 Lifecycle
docs.text:
The Lifecycle defines three persistent statuses:

Status Resolvable? Description ACTIVE Yes Normal operational state DISABLED No Temporarily disabled (can be re-enabled) DELETED No Permanently removed (cannot be restored)

EXPIRED is NOT a persistent status. It is derived at resolution time:

if expires_at and expires_at < clock:now() then
    status = "EXPIRED"  -- derived, not stored
end

State transitions:

         create
           │
           ▼
       ┌────────┐  update  ┌──────────┐
       │ ACTIVE │ ───────► │ DISABLED │
       └────────┘          └──────────┘
           │                     │
           │     update          │ update
           └──────► (back) ──────┘
           │
           │ delete
           ▼
       ┌─────────┐
       │ DELETED  │  (terminal — no transitions out)
       └─────────┘

docs.title: 3.4 Resolution
docs.text:
Resolution is the most important capability of SLDS. It is a first-class domain operation, not an alias for Repository.get().

slds:resolve(ctx, identity) -> ResolutionResult

Resolution logic:

identity → Repository.get()
  │
  ├─ Not Found ────────────────► ResolutionResult{ found = false }
  │
  ├─ status = DELETED ────────► ResolutionResult{ found = true, status = DELETED } → not resolvable
  │
  ├─ status = DISABLED ───────► ResolutionResult{ found = true, status = DISABLED } → not resolvable
  │
  ├─ expires_at < now ─────────► ResolutionResult{ found = true, status = EXPIRED } → not resolvable
  │
  └─ status = ACTIVE, not expired ─► ResolutionResult{ found = true, target = ..., status = ACTIVE }

Key principle: Resolution is Read/Resolve Semantics, not Persistence Semantics. The domain decides whether a link can be resolved — the repository merely retrieves the data.

docs.title: 3.5 ResolutionResult
docs.text:
The ResolutionResult is the output of resolution. It does not expose the internal ShortLink entity.

ResolutionResult = {
    found      = boolean,   -- was the identity found in the repository?
    namespace  = string,
    code       = string,
    target     = string|nil, -- present only if resolvable
    status     = string,     -- ACTIVE | DISABLED | DELETED | EXPIRED | NOT_FOUND
    expires_at = number|nil,
}

Why not return ShortLink directly? Returning the raw entity would leak persistence details. ResolutionResult is a stable contract that can survive entity schema changes.

docs.title: 4. Operations
docs.text:
SLDS defines four lifecycle operations (not infrastructure CRUD):

Operation Signature Description create slds:create(ctx, input) -> ShortLink, err Create a new ShortLink Identity and Target resolve slds:resolve(ctx, identity) -> ResolutionResult or nil, err Resolve an Identity; propagate infrastructure failures update slds:update(ctx, identity, patch) -> ShortLink, err Modify mutable domain properties (target, status, expires_at) delete slds:delete(ctx, identity) -> boolean, err Make an Identity permanently unresolvable

docs.title: 4.1 Create
docs.text:
Input:

{
    namespace = "default",       -- optional, defaults to "default"
    code = "a8Kx2",             -- optional; if omitted, Generator+Encoder produce one
    target = "https://...",      -- required
    expires_at = 1760000000,    -- optional
    metadata = {},              -- optional; Core MUST NOT interpret
}

Behavior:

  1. If code is provided (custom code), use it directly.
  2. If code is omitted, call Generator:generate(ctx) to get an internal ID, then Encoder:encode(id) to produce a short code.
  3. Call Repository:create(ctx, link) — uniqueness is enforced atomically by the repository.
  4. Return the created ShortLink.

docs.title: 4.2 Update
docs.text:
Patch fields — only mutable properties:

{
    target = "https://new-url.com",   -- optional
    status = "DISABLED",             -- optional
    expires_at = 1760000000,         -- optional
}

Code and namespace are immutable — updating them MUST fail with a programming error.

Only supplied non-nil target/status/expires_at fields are committed. Repository MUST atomically validate against the latest record and preserve unspecified fields; a DELETED record at commit rejects updates with nil,DELETED. Different-field changes survive and same-field changes follow commit order; application-level read-modify-write conflict detection is not promised. Failed validation MUST leave storage unchanged. A Service pre-read is insufficient to establish these guarantees.

Metadata patches are unsupported and ignored, preserving existing metadata contents. A nil expires_at patch means unchanged; this version defines no expiration-clearing sentinel. Expiration MUST be a finite number when present; equality with now remains unexpired.

docs.title: 4.3 Delete
docs.text:
Logical deletion — sets status to DELETED. The record may remain in the repository for audit purposes, but resolution MUST return "not resolvable" for deleted links.

Per RULE-006, deleted codes MUST NOT be reused by default.

docs.title: 5. Ports (Boundary Contracts)
docs.text: Ports are interface contracts, not implementations. SLDS Core depends on the interfaces; Infrastructure Adapters provide the implementations.

docs.title: 5.1 Repository Port
docs.text:
repository:create(ctx, link) -> link, err      -- create a new short link
repository:get(ctx, identity) -> link, err     -- retrieve by identity
repository:update(ctx, identity, patch) -> link, err  -- apply patch
repository:delete(ctx, identity) -> boolean, err      -- logical delete

SLDS does not care whether the repository is MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis, SQLite, or MongoDB. The repository implementation MUST enforce code uniqueness atomically (RULE-005).

docs.title: 5.2 Generator Port
docs.text:
generator:generate(ctx) -> id, err    -- generate an internal unique value

The generator produces an internal unique identifier (e.g., a sequential number, UUID, or snowflake ID). This is not the short code — the Encoder transforms it into a short code.

docs.title: 5.3 Encoder Port
docs.text:
encoder:encode(id) -> code    -- convert internal value to short code

The host MUST select a Generator/Encoder pair with compatible ID representations. Generic ports MUST NOT impose the reference adapters' numeric limit, alphabet or code length.

The encoder is a pure transformation — it does not need ctx (no I/O, no side effects). Examples: Base62 encoding, Base64 encoding, hash-based encoding.

docs.title: 6. Hooks (Extension Mechanism)
docs.text:
Hooks are the extension mechanism for observability — they are NOT part of the SLDS core domain.

slds:use(hook)

A hook is a Lua table with optional callbacks:

{
    before_create = function(ctx, input) end,
    after_create  = function(ctx, link) end,
    before_resolve = function(ctx, identity) end,
    after_resolve  = function(ctx, result) end,
    before_update = function(ctx, identity, patch) end,
    after_update  = function(ctx, link) end,
    before_delete = function(ctx, identity) end,
    after_delete  = function(ctx) end,
    on_error      = function(ctx, err) end,
}

Logger, Metrics, Tracer, and Audit are implementations of hooks, not SLDS core. SLDS provides the injection points; the application layer provides the behavior.

Key principle (RULE-007, RULE-008): Core MUST NOT require external analytics success. Hooks are synchronous observers: exceptions are isolated, but callback time adds latency. Each callback receives independent domain data snapshots; ctx is passed unchanged and MUST be treated as read-only. Mutations to domain payloads MUST NOT affect the operation, other callbacks or stored data. This is not an execution sandbox or durable event channel.

docs.title: 7. Context
docs.text:
ctx is just an API/Port parameter — it is NOT a SLDS domain concept.

It does not belong to: - Identity - ShortLink - Lifecycle - Resolution

It is not a core concept in the SLDS specification. At most, it is mentioned in the Ports/API Contract section:

ctx is a context table passed downward through a single SLDS operation execution. It may carry tenant IDs, trace spans, auth context, or other application-level data. The Repository implementation MAY use it for tenant-aware queries.

docs.title: 8. Architecture Boundary
docs.text:
Application / System
HTTP / OpenResty ──► Host → Namespace
                    Auth / Tenant / Policy
                    Rate Limit / Security
                    Cache / Metrics / Logging
                                   │
                                   │ Identity
                                   ▼
                    ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                    │            SLDS              │
                    │  Identity → ShortLink →      │
                    │  Lifecycle → Resolution →    │
                    │  ResolutionResult            │
                    │  Operations: CREATE/RESOLVE/ │
                    │  UPDATE/DELETE               │
                    │  Hooks / Ports               │
                    └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                     Repository  Generator  Encoder
                                   │
                     Infrastructure

docs.title: What Belongs to SLDS Core
docs.text: Identity, Namespace, Code, Target, Lifecycle, Expiration semantics, Resolution, ResolutionResult, Create, Update, Delete, Repository Port, Generator Port, Encoder Port, Hooks.

docs.title: What Does NOT Belong to SLDS Core
docs.text: HTTP, OpenResty, Nginx, Host/Domain, Tenant, User, Authentication, Authorization, Rate Limit, Redis, Cache, SHM, Database, Message Queue, Analytics, Click Tracking, Logger, Metrics, Tracing, Audit, URL Security, Abuse Prevention, Deployment.

docs.title: Boundary Test
docs.text: "If we remove this capability, does SLDS's Identity/Lifecycle/Resolution semantics still hold? If yes, it probably shouldn't be in Core."

docs.title: 9. Core Dependency Constraints
docs.text:
SLDS Core MUST NOT depend on:

❌ ngx
❌ ngx.req
❌ ngx.redirect
❌ ngx.header
❌ resty.redis
❌ resty.mysql
❌ lapis
❌ cjson

SLDS Core MAY use:

✅ Pure Lua (string, table, math, os, etc.)

Infrastructure Adapters (outside Core) MAY use:

OpenResty / Redis / MySQL / etc.

This constraint elevates the project from "yet another short link system" to a portable domain contract.

docs.title: 10.1 Target Validation
docs.text:
SLDS Core SHOULD validate target URL scheme at creation time:

❌ javascript:   -- MUST reject
❌ data:         -- MUST reject
❌ file:         -- MUST reject

docs.title: 10.2 SSRF Prevention
docs.text:
SLDS Core MUST NOT fetch target URLs:

❌ Do not HEAD target
❌ Do not GET target
❌ Do not validate whether target exists

Fetching the target would introduce SSRF risk into the core.

docs.title: 10.3 Open Redirect
docs.text:
Short links are inherently Open Redirects. This is a product-layer concern, not a Core bug.

Enterprise environments MAY inject a TargetPolicy:

policy:validate(target)

Allow-list example:

*.company.com
github.com
example.com

docs.title: 11. Metadata
docs.text:
SLDS Core v0.1 preserves an optional metadata = {} field on ShortLink.

Core MUST NOT interpret metadata.

metadata = {
    campaign = "black-friday",
    owner = "marketing",
    source = "internal"
}

Metadata MUST be nil or a table. Core copies raw nested table graphs at construction/export/storage boundaries, preserving cycles and shared table relationships within each snapshot and omitting metadata metatables without invoking them. Non-table leaves retain their values; mutable internals of host resources are outside this guarantee. Changes to table snapshots MUST NOT bypass Repository writes. No business schema or deep merge is defined.

Core stores and retrieves. It MUST NOT expose:

❌ link.campaign    -- business field, not domain
❌ link.owner       -- business field, not domain

docs.title: 12. Performance Targets
docs.text:
Operation Target Condition Resolve P99 < 5ms Excluding network, Core pure-memory Resolve (cache hit) P99 < 2ms Redis or local cache hit

These targets assume the Core domain logic itself is trivially fast (microseconds). The bottleneck is always I/O, which is outside Core.

docs.title: 14. Conformance Test Suite
docs.text:
See Conformance Test Specification for the full L0–L3 test matrix.

Any implementation claiming SLDS compatibility MUST pass the applicable Conformance Test Suite (RULE-010).

docs.title: SLDS Conformance Test Specification
docs.text: Field Value Status Reference suite implemented; external concurrency evidence supplied per adapter Contract version 0.1.0, hardened reference behavior (2026-10-18) Runtime matrix Lua 5.1 / Lua 5.3 / LuaJIT; Lua 5.5 is an additional local check

docs.title: Scope and evidence
docs.text:
Compatibility means passing the applicable behavioral contracts with a declared implementation, interpreter and evidence scope. A passing sequential test does not prove real database concurrency. Core is not required to add caching or tenant policy to satisfy optional extension labels.

The default suite runs the actual InMemory Repository, Sequential Generator and Base62 Encoder. Fault injection replaces specific methods or ports; it does not maintain a second mock storage implementation.

docs.title: Reusing the suite
docs.text:
The four spec/conformance/*_spec.lua files register functions from spec/conformance/suites/. An adapter author supplies a fresh fixture factory; the same assertions can be reused without copying them:

local Service = require("slds.service")
local Repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository") -- replace with your implementation
local Generator = require("slds.adapters.sequential.generator")
local Encoder = require("slds.adapters.base62.encoder")

local function make_fixture(opts)
    opts = opts or {}
    local repo = opts.repository or Repository.new()
    local gen = opts.generator or Generator.new()
    local enc = opts.encoder or Encoder.new()
    local svc = Service.new({
        repository = repo,
        generator = gen,
        encoder = enc,
        clock = opts.clock or function() return 1000000 end,
    })
    return svc, repo, gen, enc
end

require("spec.conformance.suites.l0_core")(make_fixture)
require("spec.conformance.suites.l1_lifecycle")(make_fixture)
require("spec.conformance.suites.l2_reliability")(make_fixture)
require("spec.conformance.suites.l3_extensions")(make_fixture)

Register from a Busted spec file. Every factory call must produce independent state unless a test explicitly passes a shared repository to change its clock. The factory accepts repository/generator/encoder/clock overrides for deterministic tests. The L2 interleaving tests wrap an instance's public update method; provide a writable Lua wrapper if an adapter uses userdata internally. Real external adapter tests must isolate and clean up their own records.

docs.title: Additional reference checks
docs.text:
• Identity tuples containing NUL remain distinct.
  • Input, returned and exported metadata tables do not alias stored tables; raw cyclic graphs and shared children retain their relationships within each snapshot.
  • Invalid field values and failed commits leave stored data unchanged; expected repository failures remain distinguishable from absence.
  • Hook payloads retain domain methods, have independent nested tables, and preserve nil argument gaps. ctx remains host-owned; slow callbacks still add latency.
  • Sequential/Base62 upper bounds and exhaustion are adapter-specific unit tests. A compatible string-ID pair and code longer than ten characters verify that generic Core does not impose those restrictions.

These tests are in spec/reference_adapters_spec.lua, spec/value_boundaries_spec.lua, spec/service_boundaries_spec.lua, spec/hook_observation_spec.lua, and spec/public_api_spec.lua.

docs.title: Coverage and declarations
docs.text:
Run sh scripts/test.sh followed by luacheck src/ adapters/ spec/ scripts/check-coverage.lua. The script starts with fresh LuaCov data, reports every production Lua file (including unloaded ones), and fails unless each reaches at least 95% line coverage. Project or merged coverage cannot substitute for this per-file requirement. The GitHub Actions matrix runs it for Lua 5.1, Lua 5.3 and LuaJIT.

A compatibility declaration records:

  • Suite revision and contract version.
  • Repository / Generator / Encoder combination and each applicable extension.
  • Interpreter and exact commands executed.
  • Passed scenarios, unverified scenarios and not-applicable capabilities.
  • Evidence type: sequential, deterministic interleaving, or actual external concurrency.

Do not advertise an unconditional L2/L3 badge while omitting unverified concurrency or optional extension applicability. Local reference results and migration notes are in validation.md.
